transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (AstraNova Head of Platforms), Elena Morales (FinOps), Tom Becker (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may contain errors): Walkthrough of Console route-level telemetry and cost breakdown, discuss Optimize suggestions and private deployment options.

[00:00:00] Sanjay: hey everyone thanks for joining, i see we have ravi, elena and tom — quick check, audio/video good?
[00:00:12] Ravi: yeah loud and clear, thanks for arranging this.
[00:00:18] Maya: awesome, i'll share my screen. i'm going to start in the Console overview which shows org-level usage. we'll then zoom into routes and the per-route cost attribution panel.
[00:00:35] Tom: perfect, our finance folks especially elena really want to see how calls map to costs — last quarter felt like a black box.
[00:00:42] Elena: yep, we get per-token invoices but mapping to product features is manual today.
[00:00:50] Sanjay: that's the goal here. so first slide — top-level consumption, you can filter by model, route, and timeframe. notice the left nav has Optimize suggestions which will propose batching, model variant, and quantization changes per route.
[00:01:12] Maya: jumping into routes now — here's your top ten by volume. each row shows avg latency, token count, success rate, and estimated cost. for example route /ai/summarize shows 45% of tokens and it's using a 8k-context model right now.
[00:01:36] Ravi: that might be the one...we've been passing full docs there, so makes sense. can we group by product feature, not just path?
[00:01:45] Maya: yes, tags are supported — you can map routes to product teams or features and the console will roll up costs accordingly.
[00:01:58] [00:02:05] Elena: how accurate is the cost estimate? we run on our own infra for some endpoints.
[00:02:12] Sanjay: good question — for hosted calls it's per-token billing; for dedicated/private we estimate based on your reserved capacity plus per-request overhead. accuracy improves if you provide usage CSVs or connect billing exports.
[00:02:28] Maya: and Optimize will simulate changes — like if you switch /ai/summarize to a quantized variant, we show projected cost delta and latency impact. these are heuristics but we've seen them be within 10-15% of real delta in POCs.
[00:02:45] [00:03:10] Tom: latency vs cost tradeoff matters to us. any way to set SLOs per route and have automatic routing?
[00:03:16] Maya: yes you can set policy per route — prefer low latency model, or prefer low cost — and Redwood will route to compatible variants or fallback to hosted. policies cascade and you can set canary rules.
[00:03:31] Ravi: what about caching — we have repeated prefixes across calls.
[00:03:36] Maya: we surface prefix/KV cache hit rates in the route dashboard. Optimize will recommend caching keys and TTLs. For repeated prefixes you can get 30-60% token reduction depending on conversation shape.
[00:03:50] Elena: that's promising. we have compliance concerns though — SOC2, SSO, and key management.
[00:03:58] Sanjay: on compliance, we'll share SOC2 and network diagrams. for private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM and support SAML SSO + RBAC. audit logs are available per token/action.
[00:04:15] [00:04:45] Maya: showing the cost breakdown chart — token-level vs infra amortized. infra includes dedicated pool amortization, GPU-hours, and autoscale overhead. you can toggle views.
[00:05:02] Tom: can we break down by model family? we use a mixture of open models and some in-house smaller ones.
[00:05:09] Maya: yes, model family and version are first-class dimensions. when you pin a version we track rollouts and regressions.
[00:05:20] [00:06:05] Ravi: show me a real example for a route we'd care about — maybe the question-answer route we called /qa.
[00:06:09] Maya: switching to /qa — here you can see across the last 30 days the tokens per call distribution, p95 latency, and cost per call. notice there's a spike on the 14th where token size doubled.
[00:06:25] Elena: that's the day we launched longer context in the mobile app.
[00:06:30] Maya: exactly — the console lets you pin that event and annotate releases so finance can attribute spikes to product launches.
[00:06:40] [00:07:10] Sanjay: regarding Optimize — we'll run audits on your routes and suggest batch sizes, kv-cache config, and model quantization. here's a sample recommendation: set batch target to 16 for /search to reduce GPU-hours by ~18% with minimal latency increase.
[00:07:28] Tom: do recommendations include safety checks? we care about generation quality.
[00:07:33] Maya: yes, Optimize links to eval sets — you can run a small eval comparing the baseline model vs recommended model and get quality regression alerts.
[00:07:44] [00:08:20] Elena: ok, when you say "reduce GPU-hours" how do you monetize that in the invoice? we need a line-by-line forecast.
[00:08:28] Sanjay: we'll produce a forecast that maps your current usage to projected spend under different Optimize configs. that'll be the ROI spreadsheet i'll send. it includes per-route delta and percent savings.
[00:08:40] [00:09:00] Ravi: i heard mention of model fallbacks and routing — if a requested model isn't available can it fallback to cheaper one automatically?
[00:09:07] Maya: yep you can set fallback chains and region-based preferences. for strict SLOs you can also set automatic alerting and circuit-breaker behavior.
[00:09:19] [00:10:05] Tom: about private deployment — if we want the control plane in our VPC and inference on-prem, how much operational lift is on us?
[00:10:13] Sanjay: for Private we provide a customer-managed control plane with an on-prem agent. we hand over deployment manifests and a runbook; Redwood supports initial setup and offers an enterprise support package. ops work depends on your infra maturity.
[00:10:27] Maya: we also have a hybrid option where sensitive routes run in your private pool and less sensitive in hosted. Console will show unified telemetry.
[00:10:40] [00:11:00] Elena: can we restrict who sees cost vs who sees telemetry?
[00:11:05] Maya: RBAC is flexible — you can create roles like FinOps Viewer, Platform Admin, and restrict token-level details.
[00:11:12] [00:12:20] Ravi: demo the per-route alerting rules please.
[00:12:25] Maya: sure — creating a rule: pick route, set condition (p95 latency > 700ms for 5 minutes) and select notification (pagerduty/slack/email). you can also auto-trigger a failover to a cheaper model if latency SLA is met.
[00:12:45] [00:13:30] Sanjay: quick aside — competitors like MajorCloudAI and Anthropic have dashboards but not the same route-level cost attribution tied to Optimize suggestions we've built. internal platforms often lack the Optimize kit and model quantization guidance.
[00:13:50] Elena: understood. pricing model question: how is Dedicated invoiced vs Hosted?
[00:13:57] Sanjay: hosted is usage-based; dedicated is reserved capacity monthly with overage rates and optional burst pricing. private combines a platform fee. we'll put exact numbers in the ROI sheet.
[00:14:12] [00:15:00] Maya: walking through an example: change /ai/summarize to a 4-bit quantized variant, enable prefix caching, and reduce max tokens where possible. Console shows projected 42% token cost reduction and 8% p95 latency increase, with notes to run evals.
[00:15:20] Ravi: 42% is interesting — would like to see that applied to our top 5 routes.
[00:15:25] Sanjay: we can run a scoped POC for top 5 routes and provide dashboards with before/after metrics.
[00:15:34] [00:16:40] Tom: about audit logs — how granular are they? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
[00:16:45] Maya: logs include request id, route, model version, timestamps, and truncated payloads if you opt in; full payload storage is optional and encrypted if you choose that.
[00:16:57] Elena: is there a retention policy we can set per workspace?
[00:17:02] Sanjay: yes retention is configurable — default 90 days, can be extended with enterprise plan.
[00:17:10] [00:18:00] Ravi: any out-of-the-box connectors to our billing system?
[00:18:05] Maya: you can export per-route CSVs, or use our billing API to pull usage programmatically. there's also a Snowflake connector in beta.
[00:18:20] Elena: the Snowflake connector is appealing.
[00:18:24] [00:19:10] Sanjay: quick Q to the group — what's your timeline for making a decision?
[00:19:16] Tom: ideally before our end-of-year budget freeze, so mid-december decision window.
[00:19:23] Elena: that works. once we see numbers from the ROI sheet and audit notes we'll be comfortable.
[00:19:30] [00:20:00] Maya: wrapping up the Console UI demo — there's a routes heatmap, a cost-attribution waterfall, and a model-variant comparison tool. also a section for Optimize 'playbook' which lists recommended actions per route.
[00:20:18] Ravi: can the playbook be exported as a checklist for our SREs?
[00:20:22] Maya: yes, exportable and you can convert items into tasks that sync to Jira.
[00:20:30] [00:21:00] Sanjay: for next steps: we'll produce the ROI sheet, share SOC2 and private deployment notes, and set up a POC scoping call.
[00:21:10] Elena: can you give us trial Console access scoped to FinOps so i can poke around?
[00:21:15] Sanjay: yes i'll enable a limited trial for elena today.
[00:21:25] [00:30:00] -- (silent demo navigation and screen sharing for ~9 minutes where Maya flips through route dashboards and Optimize recommendations, occasional questions) --
[00:40:05] Ravi: on the sample forecast, can you normalize for our hybrid setup where some routes are on-prem?
[00:40:12] Maya: yes we can model hybrid by assigning routes to pools — private vs hosted — and the forecast reflects reserved capacity amortization for private.
[00:40:40] Elena: any gotchas around KV cache consistency across regions?
[00:40:45] Maya: recommended pattern is local KV per region; global sync causes latency. Optimize will call that out and quantify cross-region hit rate effects.
[00:41:03] Tom: aside — do you support custom model binaries? we have a small fine-tuned transformer.
[00:41:09] Sanjay: we support onboarding custom models; there's a verification step and we run perf profiles. for private you can keep model artifacts in your repos.
[00:41:22] [00:45:00] -- brief discussion on SLAs, support tiers, and pricing --
[00:47:10] Ravi: last question, what does the POC look like?
[00:47:15] Maya: a two-week scoped POC: we'll instrument 3-5 routes, run Optimize audits, implement caching/batching changes, and produce a before/after dashboard and cost forecast. minimal infra changes required for hosted; private will need an initial setup window.
[00:47:35] Elena: good. please include one quality regression check in the POC.
[00:47:40] Maya: noted.
[00:50:00] Sanjay: thanks all — recap: Sanjay to send ROI + enable trial; Maya to share SOC2 and deployment checklist; schedule POC scoping next week.
[00:50:20] Tom: thanks folks, good demo.
[00:50:30] Ravi: thanks, bye.
[00:51:00] Elena: bye.

Recorded transcript end.
